nodes.label: Subagent output compression saves main context
nodes.rationale: Subagent tool results are injected into main context verbatim; a vanilla Explore returning 2k tokens of prose costs 2k tokens of main-context budget every time, while cavecrew-investigator returns ~700 tokens for the same finding. Across 20 delegations in one session that is the difference between context exhaustion and finishing the task.
nodes.norm_label: subagent output compression saves main context

nodes.label: Auto-Clarity rule (caveman-commit)
nodes.rationale: Always include a body for breaking changes, security fixes, data migrations, and reverts — future debuggers need the context, so these must never be compressed into subject-only.

nodes.label: Snyk High Risk rating (false positive)
nodes.rationale: Snyk flags caveman-compress High Risk due to static-analysis heuristics on subprocess usage and file read/write. It's a false positive: the subprocess call uses a fixed argument list with no shell interpolation, file content goes via stdin, and the skill only reads/writes the user-specified path plus its .original.md backup.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md compression saves per-session tokens
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md loads on every session start, so a 1000-token file costs tokens every session; over 100 sessions that's 100,000 tokens of pure overhead. Caveman-compress cuts ~46% of that by compressing prose while preserving code blocks, URLs, file paths, and structure exactly.

nodes.label: Auto-Clarity rule (caveman-review)
nodes.rationale: Terse mode is dropped for CVE-class security findings, architectural disagreements, and onboarding contexts where the author needs the 'why' — a normal paragraph is written for those, then terse mode resumes.

nodes.label: Stats read from session log, not AI-estimated
nodes.rationale: Numbers come directly from the JSONL session log on disk rather than the model computing or estimating them, so the reported token usage is a real receipt, not a guess.
nodes.norm_label: stats read from session log, not ai-estimated

nodes.label: Auto-Clarity rule (caveman)
nodes.rationale: Caveman mode drops to normal prose for security warnings, irreversible-action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment ambiguity risks misread, cases where compression itself creates technical ambiguity, and when the user repeats a question — then resumes caveman afterward.
